instructions.purpose: Schedule one-time events that fire once at a specific future date and time. Use this tool when the user wants a reminder, alarm, timer, or notification that should not repeat.

tool.name: schedule-once
tool.description: Creates a one-time cron job identified by a unique name that fires at the provided fireAt timestamp. The job removes itself after firing. Also stores either direct reminder text or LLM regeneration data with a fallback message. Returns the scheduled job details including the fire time.

datetime_rules.rule: Use the current time context from the conversation to resolve relative times like "in 2 minutes", "tomorrow", or "tonight"
Use the configured timezone when interpreting relative or local times: {{config.ai.instructions.timezone}}
For relative requests, compute fireAt from the provided current local time, not from memory or guessed time
Convert the final scheduled time to an ISO 8601 timestamp for fireAt
If the user's requested date or time is ambiguous, ask a clarifying question before calling this tool
Never schedule a fireAt in the past

usage_rules.rule: Always confirm the exact one-time fire date and time with the user before calling this tool
Use this tool for non-repeating reminders; use schedule-recurring when the user asks for repetition
Choose clear, descriptive names for jobs so they can be easily referenced later
If a one-time job with the same name already exists, set overwrite to true only if the user explicitly agrees to replace it
Always provide reminderText for direct reminders, or reminderPromptData plus reminderFallbackText for generated reminders
Pass reminderPromptData as a serialized JSON string, not as a nested object
Inform the user of the scheduled fire time after successfully scheduling

example.context: User says: "Remind me tomorrow at 9 to call the dentist"
example.reasoning: One reminder at a specific future time, so schedule a one-time job.

example.context: User says: "Za 20 minut przypomnij mi wyjąć pranie"
example.reasoning: A relative timer that fires once.

example.context: User says: "Tomorrow afternoon remind me to prepare for the meeting, make it motivating"
